Audit readiness built into routine, not added before inspection

Staff certification and progression paths

Team building in existing brigades, not only new ones

preopening.title: How I open a kitchen
preopening.lead: 14 openings: restaurants, hotels and river cruise ships. Each one is different, but the flow is the same: from concept to a stable service, with a team that is ready on day one.

meta.v: Restaurants, hotels and river cruise ships

preopening.ganttNote: A typical flow. Phase length depends on the size and format of the venue.

phases.label: Concept and menu
points: Kitchen concept aligned with the venue and its guests
Menu, recipes and costing: food cost is known from day one
Menu engineering before the first pan is bought

phases.label: Kitchen and equipment
points: Workflow: receiving, storage, prep, service and dishwashing
Equipment specification, from heavy equipment to smallwares
Tracking delivery and installation with contractors and technicians

phases.label: Team and organisation
points: Org chart and a job description for every position
Recruitment and selection
Shift planning and labour cost plan

phases.label: Suppliers and purchasing
points: Selecting and contracting suppliers for food and equipment
Product specifications, prices and delivery terms
Opening order and stock plan

phases.label: Standards and systems
points: Standard recipes and plate photos
Operating procedures and HACCP plan
Systems for ordering, inventory and cost control

phases.label: Training and competencies
points: Competency framework for every position
Day-by-day training plan
Assessment and certification before opening

phases.label: Rehearsals and soft opening
points: Master plan and rehearsals with service, stewarding, purchasing and engineering
Mock services at real pace
Soft opening and fixes before the official opening

phases.label: Stabilisation
points: Tracking food cost, waste and ticket times
Feedback from guests and the team
Refining the menu and processes in the first weeks

formats.d: One concept and a shorter cycle. The focus is on the menu, the team and the first weeks of service.
Several outlets at once: restaurant, bar, banqueting, room service and staff dining, aligned with every department.
Limited space, sourcing port by port and the whole team on board from the first day of the season.
